question: One reason why Mendel was successful in discovering the laws governing inheritance of traits was __________.

options.text: he was trained in scientific methods
he kept numerical count of the progeny
he used plants instead of animals
he used his knowledge of evolutionary processes

solution:
The correct answer is __**he kept numerical count of the progeny**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Mendel chose to study pea plants (Pisum sativum) for his experiments, and this choice proved to be highly advantageous. Pea plants exhibit several characteristics that made them ideal for genetic studies:

 
• **Clearly defined traits:** Pea plants display a variety of easily distinguishable traits, such as flower color (purple or white), seed shape (round or wrinkled), and plant height (tall or short). This clear-cut distinction allowed Mendel to accurately observe and categorize the inheritance patterns of these traits.
 
• **Self-pollination and controlled cross-pollination:** Pea plants can self-pollinate, meaning that pollen from the same plant can fertilize its own ovules. However, they can also be easily cross-pollinated by manually transferring pollen from one plant to another. This control over pollination allowed Mendel to precisely manipulate the breeding process and study the inheritance of specific traits.
 
• **Short life cycle and high fecundity:** Pea plants have a relatively short life cycle, allowing Mendel to conduct multiple generations of experiments within a reasonable timeframe. Additionally, they produce a large number of offspring, providing ample data for statistical analysis.
